name: Weri
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 9 other works read were silent
catalog_quote: 3.5. Stress. Stress in Weri is non-phonemic, occurring on the final syllable of a word. Each preceding alternate syllable carries a secondary stress. Often in four and five syllable words the stress on the antepenultimate syllable is equal to or heavier than that on the ultimate.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict' final primary with alternating preceding secondaries (alternating stress from the right) matches Boxwell & Boxwell 1966:88 sec. 3.5 exactly, verified verbatim in the PDF we hold/text, and is restated by Boxwell 1992 OPD ('Stress is non-phonemic, occurring on the final syllable of a word'), also. These are the only two phonology descriptions of Weri that exist per Glottolog 5.1 and SIL's full Weri resource list; all secondary treatments (Hayes 1981, Bailey 1995, Gordon 2002, StressTyp2) trace to the 1966 paper. The record's 'quote'/'cite'/'grade' fields are empty while the verified quotation sits in 'the domain quotation'/'sources'; promote it to the primary quote with locator 'Boxwell & Boxwell 1966:88 sec. 3.5' and add the 1992 OPD as a confirming second source. One nuance worth a caution note rather than a reclassify: the 1966 text says that in 4-5 syllable words antepenult stress is 'often

sources.quote: "3.5. Stress. Stress in Weri is non-phonemic, occurring on the final syllable of a word. Each preceding alternate syllable carries a secondary stress. Often in four and five syllable words the stress on the antepenultimate syllable is equal to or heavier than that on the ultimate." (Boxwell & Boxwell 1966:88; followed by examples /ŋintíp/ [ŋin'tɨp] 'bee', [kúlí'pú] 'hair of arm', [úlúá'mɨt] 'mist', [ákūnētē'pal] 'times')
